title: JS API E2E Electron cleanup fails on Windows - Permission denied removing locked electron.exe/dll
signature: rm cannot remove electron.exe Permission denied|Flaky Test

failed_jobs.name: JS API (26)
failed_jobs.symptom: E2E of openvino-node package step fails - electron.exe Permission denied during cleanup

key_errors: Step 'E2E of openvino-node package' failed in job 'JS API (26)'
Known pattern: rm cannot remove electron.exe: Permission denied (locked process on Windows runner)
Step conclusion: failure; subsequent steps (E2E cmd, Create package dir, Test installation) all skipped
root_cause: The Electron process started during the E2E test is not fully terminated before the cleanup phase attempts to delete it. On Windows runners, a running or recently-exited process keeps a lock on its executable, causing the `rm` or cleanup step to fail with 'Permission denied'. This is a well-known transient runner-side race condition that does not affect functional correctness and resolves on retry.
reproduction_steps: Run the JS API E2E test on a Windows runner. The failure is intermittent and depends on process cleanup timing.
recommended_actions: Re-add PR #36937 to the merge queue - this is a transient flaky test unrelated to the PR changes
Long-term: add a retry/kill loop in the E2E cleanup step to forcefully terminate electron.exe before removing files
Consider using taskkill /F /IM electron.exe before rm in the Windows E2E cleanup step
prevention_strategies: Add a pre-cleanup step in the JS API E2E workflow that forcefully kills any lingering electron.exe processes on Windows (e.g., `taskkill /F /IM electron.exe || true`).
historical_context: This exact failure has been recorded 12 times since 2026-07-09 (pattern hash 85df26485ff568d8). All prior occurrences were resolved by re-running or re-queueing the affected PR. Affected PRs include #36905, #36933, #36884, and others.
